title: Understanding Ruby Blocks
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of understanding ruby blocks in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply understanding ruby blocks in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to blocks as reusable control patterns and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Understanding Ruby Blocks through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding understanding ruby blocks helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Understanding Ruby Blocks helps you reason about what a block represents. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: What a block represents. Then connect it to Passing behavior to methods. The remaining syllabus points—Blocks as reusable control patterns—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Understanding Ruby Blocks
content_blocks.code:
def around
  puts "start"
  yield
  puts "finish"
end
around { puts "work" }

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.title: Mixing too many concerns
items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports understanding ruby blocks. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for understanding ruby blocks using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Blocks as reusable control patterns), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.title: Run, troubleshoot, and reset
content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. If the command fails, confirm `ruby --version`, inspect the full error message, and verify that required standard-library or gem dependencies are installed. Reset by removing temporary files created by your experiment and returning the code to the smallest reproducible example.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain understanding ruby blocks, identify its place in blocks, procs, lambdas, and closures, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
